derived_phases.note: W=|⟨(σx-σy)⊗σz⟩|. Product states reach √2, so W>1 does not prove entanglement. Valid pure-state test: concurrence > 0, i.e. Δφ_LR+Δφ_RL != 2πn.

quoted_phases.note: W=|⟨(σx-σy)⊗σz⟩|. Product states reach √2, so W>1 does not prove entanglement. Valid pure-state test: concurrence > 0, i.e. Δφ_LR+Δφ_RL != 2πn.

witness.discrepancy: Bose quotes Δφ_LR∼−0.2, Δφ_RL∼0.7, W∼1.16. With V=−Gmm/r and the stated geometry we get Δφ_LR=+0.126, Δφ_RL=−0.440 (signs from attraction). The magnitudes of the unsubtracted phases are φ(d)=0.352, φ_closest=0.791, φ_farthest=0.226, so their −0.2 and 0.7 look like rounded unsubtracted φ_LR and φ_RL (0.226 and 0.791) with an unexplained minus on the far arm, not the subtracted Δφ of their eq. (2). The written witness W=|⟨σx⊗σz⟩−⟨σy⊗σz⟩| equals 0.107 (derived phases) or 0.330 (their quoted phases), not 1.16. We could not reconstruct 1.16 from the written definition. Independently, W>1 is not a valid entanglement test: product states reach W=√2. A valid test for this family is concurrence C=|sin((Δφ_LR+Δφ_RL)/2)|, which is 0.156 (derived) or 0.247 (quoted phases). Both are entangled, just not by the W>1 argument as written.

casimir.formula: U_CP=-(23 ħ c /4π) [R^3 (ε-1)/(ε+2)]^2 / r^7  (SI, retarded two-sphere)
casimir.note: Bose says CP is a tenth of gravity at 200 μm. We get 0.050 with their (m,R) pair, or 0.023 if m is taken from diamond density at R=1 μm. Same order; the 0.1 is a rounded estimate and their (m,R) pair is not density-consistent (1 μm of diamond is 1.47e-14 kg).

gradient_and_drop.note: Bose quotes 1e6 T/m and g_grav~1e-16 m/s^2; both match. 3.5 s free fall is 60 m, so drop tower or space.

decoherence_at_bose_point.note_coll: At P=1e-15 Pa with geometric πR² collisions on a 1 μm sphere, the decoherence time is 2.8e3 s for N2 at 300 K and 62 s for N2 at 0.15 K (DERIVED). Both are comfortably longer than the 3.5 s drop: Γ t = 0.0013 (300 K) or 0.056 (0.15 K). Bose’s “same order as 3.5 s” is therefore pessimistic by 1–3 orders at this P. Γ t = 1 at 300 K would require P ≈ 8e-13 Pa, still very good vacuum but not XHV.
decoherence_at_bose_point.bb_note: At 0.15 K, λ_th≈1.5 cm ≫ 250 μm, so photon scattering is in the soft quadratic regime and Γ t is ~10^{-17}, negligible, as Bose says. Room-temperature radiation would destroy the superposition in nanoseconds (resolution-limited scattering rate ~10^{11}/s on a 1 μm dielectric). Internal temperature must also be cryogenic, or the object’s own thermal emission does the same. The environment can actually be several kelvin before photon scattering competes with 3.5 s (see T_env_max).

gap_orders.note: Mass gap vs matter-wave interference is ~8 orders (Fein 25 kDa) or ~7.5 (Na 172 kDa). The cooled-nanoparticle mass gap is only ~4 orders, but those particles are in a ground-state oscillator state with Δx ~ picometres, not a 250 μm cat. Phase scales as m² t / d, so the phase gap is much larger than the mass gap (see phase_at_records).

groups_CITED: Bose / UCL and the QGEM white-paper consortium (arXiv:2509.01586, 2025): building traps for micron diamonds / nanodiamonds; first spatial superpositions expected at 10–1000 fm, then push to 10–100 μm; two-diamond setups and EM screening in parallel. “Significant steps … within the next decade” with sufficient resources. Underground lab may be needed for vibration / GGN.
Folman (Ben-Gurion): Stern–Gerlach interferometry with atoms already demonstrated (e.g. Science Advances 7, eabg2879 (2021)); contributing to the spin-based diamond pathway (white paper coauthor).

Aspelmeyer (Vienna / IQOQI): levitated optomechanics, ground-state cooling (Delić 2020); smallest source-mass gravity measurement, 90.7 mg test / 92.1 mg source gold spheres (Westphal et al., Nature 591, 225 (2021)). Public timeline ~15 years for a viable entanglement experiment (New Scientist, 12 May 2025), described as a self-imposed deadline.
Geraci (now Northwestern / formerly UNR): optically levitated nanoparticles and short-range gravity; Bose 2017 and white-paper coauthor.

Arndt (Vienna): heaviest matter-wave interference — 25 kDa molecules (Fein 2019) and 172 kDa sodium clusters (Pedalino et al., arXiv:2507.21211). Complementary mass path, still many orders below QGEM.
Others on the white paper: Ulbricht (Southampton), Barker (UCL), Kim (Imperial), Milburn, Kent, Purdy, Dutt, and several theory groups.
alternatives_CITED: Krisnanda, Tham, Paternostro & Paterek, arXiv:1906.08808: optomechanical (always-trapped) masses, or masses released from traps. Trapped version wants LIGO-like mirrors plus squeezing or very long coherence; released masses can be lighter. No macroscopic cat is required in their Gaussian-state analysis.

Pedernales & Plenio, arXiv:2311.04745 (and earlier Pedernales/Plenio nanodiamond work): force sensitivity of delocalised mechanics is set by spatial delocalisation; cat states and momentum-squeezed Gaussians entangle at the same rate if equally delocalised. This is the “mass / delocalisation determines the rate” alternative to spin-SG cats, not a different gravitational mechanism.
Casimir screening (van de Kamp, Marshman, Bose & Mazumdar, arXiv:2006.06931; white paper): a conducting plate can suppress EM backgrounds and may allow a smaller d, lowering the mass or time demand.

timeline_CITED.white_paper_2025: Significant steps toward QGEM possible in the next decade (i.e. mid-2030s), not a claim that the witness will be measured by then. First milestone is any spatial superposition of a nanoparticle, even 10–1000 fm.
timeline_CITED.aspelmeyer_2025: ~15 years from May 2025, i.e. around 2040, for a viable experiment; self-imposed. He also said a strictly spacelike-separated, “foolproof” version is not realistic on any human timescale (New Scientist, 12 May 2025).
timeline_CITED.honest_read: No group has a 10^{-14} kg object in a ~250 μm superposition for seconds, which is the actual requirement. The mass gap in interference is 7–8 orders; the phase gap is larger because Δφ ∝ m². A completed BMV test before the late 2030s would be a surprise. Collapse-model tests with a single large superposition can come earlier and already matter.

section3_status.ggn_CITED: Toroš, Marshman, Mazumdar & Bose, Phys. Rev. Research 3, 023178 (2021), arXiv:2007.15029: gravity-gradient noise is not a fundamental blocker. Seismic/atmospheric are small; human/vehicle/aircraft can be kept out by access restrictions of about 2 m / 10 m / 60 m. Underground helps. This is a site and isolation problem, not a no-go.

positive_result.locc: Marletto–Vedral / Bose: if two quantum systems become entangled and the only interaction is gravitational, and if that interaction is mediated (not action at a distance), then the mediator cannot be a classical channel, because LOCC cannot create entanglement. That is the clean core.
positive_result.what_it_shows: It shows that gravity can entangle quantum matter, so gravity is not a purely classical communication channel between quantum systems. In linearized GR language, Bose et al. argue this needs off-diagonal amplitudes in the gravitational-field coherent-state basis.
what_it_does_not_show: It does not detect gravitons as particles, and does not reach Planck-scale quantum gravity.

Fragkos, Kopp & Pikovski, AVS Quantum Sci. 4, 045601 (2023), arXiv:2206.00558: the entanglement is generated by the Newtonian interaction (a constraint / Poisson-gauge term), which can be written as a non-local stress-energy coupling with no local mediator. Relativity does not force a unique local-channel reading. A positive result would still be the first test of how a spatial superposition sources a Newtonian field, which has never been done.

Anastopoulos & Hu: the 2018 arXiv comment (1804.11315) was withdrawn (arXiv lists it as withdrawn; copyright, not a retraction of the scientific point). The later paper “Gravity, Quantum Fields and Quantum Information”, arXiv:2202.02789, argues that in the weak-field Newtonian limit the potential is slaved to the mass density, so seeing entanglement from that term does not by itself prove that the true radiative degrees of freedom (gravitons) are quantum.

A laboratory BMV protocol with d~200 μm and t~2.5 s is not spacelike separated (d/c ~ 0.7 ps). A classical or quantum non-gravitational process that can act over that time is not forbidden by causality; it has to be excluded by shielding and control experiments. Aspelmeyer’s “foolproof” spacelike version is far harder.

positive_entanglement: Fully classical gravitational channels (gravity as LOCC) and classical-only Newton potential acting as a c-number field with no quantum coherence.

Objective collapse models that would have already decohered a 10^{-14} kg / 250 μm superposition on the 1 s timescale (Diósi–Penrose and similar), if such a superposition is first created at all. Aspelmeyer, C. R. Physique 27, 1 (2026) argues a positive GIE result rules out current gravitational-collapse models once lab constraints are included.

Oppenheim-type postquantum classical gravity is not automatically killed by a GIE detection in every formulation; the debate is live (see critiques and later CQ papers). A detected entanglement with coherence surviving the CQ tradeoff would put severe pressure on those models, but we do not claim a theorem here.
negative_or_null: A null result at insufficient mass/time/vacuum does not kill quantum gravity; it is just a failed attempt.

A null result in a regime where a quantum Newtonian interaction should have entangled the masses, after EM backgrounds are demonstrated to be under control, would be a genuine crisis for standard quantized linearized gravity and would favour collapse models or a classical gravitational channel.

oppenheim.statement: Oppenheim et al., Nat. Commun. 14, 7910 (2023), arXiv:2203.01982: any consistent classical-gravity / quantum-matter coupling has a tradeoff. Long quantum coherence requires spacetime diffusion (noise in the metric / Newtonian potential). Precision mass/acceleration measurements cap the diffusion from above; matter-wave coherence caps the decoherence rate and so floors the diffusion. The two together squeeze the theory.

oppenheim.janse2024_cite: Janse et al., Phys. Rev. Research 6, 033076 (2024), arXiv:2403.08912: the Cavendish figure of merit FOM=σa² N ΔT used by Oppenheim is 1e14 m²/s³; Gisler et al. nanowire (m_eff=9.3e-15 kg) improves FOM by ~15 orders (absolute accel. noise on Earth). LISA Pathfinder and atom interferometry look even better but are differential / relative measurements, and atom interferometers are also the experiments that set the lower bound, so using them on both sides is questionable (their caveat). We therefore only scale the upper bounds by 1e-15 as a CITED estimate for the best uncontroversial tightening, and do not claim the remaining models are ruled out.
oppenheim.verdict: Ultra-local continuous noise (D2 δ(x−y) everywhere) is already excluded by Oppenheim’s own conservative Cavendish-vs-fullerene squeeze: we recompute lower/upper ≈ 10^{-24} / 10^{-41} kg² s m^{-3}, a 17-order overlap. The ultra-local discrete and non-local continuous (Diósi–Penrose-like) models are not excluded on those conservative numbers (gaps of tens of orders). Janse et al. 2024 tighten the upper side by ~15 orders with modern absolute force-noise data, which shrinks but does not close those gaps if one refuses differential measurements. This is the nearer-term test: it uses existing torsion, nanowire, and interferometry data, and improves every time a quieter force sensor or a heavier coherent superposition is published. It does not require two 10^{-14} kg cats.

useful: Independent decoherence budgets and design optimisation: map (m, R, d, Δx, t, P, T_gas, T_env, T_int, gas species, dielectric function) to Δφ, concurrence, and Γ t, including Casimir-safe d and optional conductive shields (van de Kamp et al.). This is finite-dimensional numerical work and is exactly what proposals need checked by a second calculation.

Recompute and stress-test published feasibility numbers. We already found that the headline W∼1.16 does not follow from the written witness and quoted phases, and that Bose’s CP “tenth” is ~0.05 with the standard SI formula. An open, cited errata/clarification note would be useful.

Oppenheim squeeze with current data: update the lower bound with each new interference mass (25 kDa, 172 kDa, and whatever comes next) and the upper bound with each new low-force-noise measurement, being explicit about absolute vs differential and about the wavepacket volume. Janse et al. already started this; it is ongoing and checkable.

Open problems listed in the 2025 QGEM white paper (arXiv:2509.01586) that are calculation- or simulation-heavy: EM screening / patch potentials, Casimir with a real finite-conductivity plate between two diamonds, surface-spin noise on nanodiamond (they quote 0.01 spins/nm² ⇒ >10^4 unpaired spins on a nanodiamond), gravity-gradient and vibration transfer functions, motional dynamical decoupling sequences, and whether dark-matter or collapse-model decoherence would dominate before gravity entangles.
not_useful: Inventing a new unified-field picture without a number that one of these experiments can kill.
Trying to simulate Planck-scale quantum gravity or a first-principles graviton S-matrix for this apparatus: the entanglement, if it happens, is a low-energy Newtonian / linearized-GR effect.
